- Several biomechanical considerations need to be taken into account when selecting exercises for a hypertrophy-oriented program. These include length-tension relationship, training angle, plane of movement, spacing of hands and feet, and exercise type.
- The application of biomechanical principles to exercise selection is specific to a given muscle, its architecture, and the joint at which it originates. Combining exercises based on applied anatomy and kinesiology is essential to ensuring the complete development of the major musculature.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 8: Program Design for Maximal Hypertrophy
